title: Invariant closed rank filtration of a finite groupoid
statement: Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], and assume that $s,t:R\to U$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then there are closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] $U=Z_0\supseteq Z_1\supseteq Z_2\supseteq\cdots$ with $\bigcap_{n\geq0}|Z_n|=\varnothing$, such that $s^{-1}(Z_n)=t^{-1}(Z_n)$ as closed subschemes of $R$ for every $n$. For every integer $r\geq1$, put $D_r=Z_{r-1}\setminus Z_r$, the open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] of $Z_{r-1}$ obtained by removing $|Z_r|$. The projection $R\times_{s,U}D_r\to D_r$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. No Noetherian, quasi-compact, flatness or finite-presentation assumption on $U,s,t$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $E=s_*\mathcal O_R$. It is finite-type quasi-coherent and $s$ is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Form $I_n=\operatorname{Fit}_n(E)$ and its closed subscheme $Z_n$ using [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-pullback]. Locally, for a surjection $A^m\twoheadrightarrow E(V)$ on $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $I_n(V)$ consists of the $(m-n)$-minors of kernel rows, with unit ideal for $n\geq m$. Laplace expansion expresses each size $k$ minor as a sum of entries times size $k-1$ minors, so $I_n\subseteq I_{n+1}$ and $Z_{n+1}\subseteq Z_n$ as closed subschemes. Every point has an affine neighbourhood with a finite such generating family by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a). On it $I_m=\mathcal O$, hence $Z_m$ is empty there. Thus $\bigcap_{n\geq0}|Z_n|=\varnothing$, without a global generator bound.

source.place: 0AB9, first paragraph; divisors.tex 05P8(1), with the affine minor construction 0C3C.

proof.text: The identity section satisfies $se=\mathrm{id}_U$ by [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], so on every affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U$ the structure map $A\to B=E(V)$ has a retraction $B\to A$ and is injective. Choose $m$ generators $b_j$ of $B$. Any $m$ kernel rows give a square matrix $N$ with $N(b_j)_j=0$. Multiplying by its adjugate shows $\det(N)b_j=0$ for every $j$, hence $\det(N)$ annihilates $1_B$, since the $b_j$ generate $B$. Injectivity of $A\to B$ gives $\det(N)=0$. All generating minors of $I_0$ therefore vanish. The affine description in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-pullback] gives $I_0=0$ and $Z_0=U$. This also handles an empty affine open (its ring is zero).

source.place: 0AB9, omitted detail establishing Z_0=U; replace the printed O_S summand by O_U.

proof.text: Let $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$ and $Q=R\times_{s,U,s}R$, both over $R$ by the second projections $p_2,q_2$. The first clause of [lem-a1-groupoid-source-pullback-translation] gives an isomorphism $F:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ over $R$, $F(a,b)=(c(a,b),b)$, with inverse $(d,b)\mapsto(c(d,i(b)),b)$. We use this clause without any local-freeness assumption. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](2) to $s$ along $t$ and along $s$. It identifies $t^*E$ with $p_{2,*}\mathcal O_P$ and $s^*E$ with $q_{2,*}\mathcal O_Q$. Pullback of functions along the displayed isomorphism over $R$ identifies these two direct-image algebras, hence $t^*E\cong s^*E$ as $\mathcal O_R$-modules.

source.place: 0AB9, comparison through the two lower Cartesian squares of more-groupoids.tex equation-diagram; groupoids.tex 02YE and coherent.tex 02KG.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-pullback] to $s,t$ and $E$: the closed subschemes $s^{-1}(Z_n)$ and $t^{-1}(Z_n)$ are respectively the closed Fitting subschemes for $s^*E$ and $t^*E$. Under the isomorphism of Step 3, a generating surjection to one module becomes a generating surjection to the other with exactly the same kernel, so their kernel-minor ideals agree on every affine open. Their defining ideals, and therefore their closed subschemes of $R$, are equal. This is scheme-theoretic invariance, even for nonreduced $U$.

source.place: 0AB9, invariance paragraph; divisors.tex 0C3D, using invariance of kernel presentations under a module isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix $r\geq1$ and put $W_r=U\setminus|Z_r|$. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally](1), $E|_{W_r}$ is locally generated by at most $r$ sections. The subscheme $D_r=Z_{r-1}\setminus|Z_r|$ is the closed subscheme of $W_r$ defined by $I_{r-1}|_{W_r}$: on affine charts both descriptions are the quotient by this ideal followed by restriction to the open complement. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-pullback] for the open inclusion $W_r\to U$, this ideal is $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(E|_{W_r})$. Its image after pullback to $D_r$ is zero, since its elements map to zero in the quotient rings. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-generators-fitting-pullback-criterion] to $E|_{W_r}$ and $D_r\to W_r$. Thus $E|_{D_r}$, meaning ordinary pullback, is locally free of constant rank $r$.

Put $f_r:R\times_{s,U}D_r\to D_r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1), $f_r$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](2), $f_{r,*}\mathcal O\cong E|_{D_r}$. Choose an affine open cover $(V_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a)$ of $D_r$ trivializing this rank-$r$ module (Step 5). Affineness gives $f_r^{-1}(V_a)=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$; taking sections of the trivialization gives an $A_a$-module basis of $B_a$ with $r$ elements. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum], $f_r$ over $V_a$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. At every $v\in V_a$, [lem-pc-finite-affine-fibre-sections] identifies its fibre algebra with $B_a\otimes_{A_a}\kappa(v)\cong\kappa(v)^r$, as $\kappa(v)$-vector spaces, so its degree is $r$. The open inclusions $V_a\to D_r$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and cover $D_r$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-etale-descent] to conclude that $f_r$ is finite locally free of degree $r$. This includes empty $D_r$ with its empty cover. Steps 1--5 supply the other assertions.
